body:
Hi @dgengtek, I've been trying to reproduce this locally but so far have been unable to.

```
starship on  master [⇡] is 📦 v0.44.0 via 🦀 v1.45.0 
✦ ❯ ln -s ~/.config/starship.toml ~/.config/starship_link.toml
~/s/r/starship on  master [⇡1] is 📦 v0.44.0 via 🦀 v1.45.0 
✦ ❯ STARSHIP_CONFIG=~/.config/starship_link.toml STARSHIP_LOG=debug starship prompt
 DEBUG starship::config > STARSHIP_CONFIG is set: 
/home/andy/.config/starship_link.toml
 DEBUG starship::config > Config parsed: 
Table({"add_newline": Boolean(false), "battery": Table({}), "directory": Table({"fish_style_pwd_dir_length": Integer(1)}), "git_status": Table({"show_sync_count": Boolean(true)}), "kubernetes": Table({"disabled": Boolean(false)}), "python": Table({"python_binary": String("python3")})})
...
```

Can you try running `STARSHIP_LOG=debug starship prompt` and paste the output here.

Hi @andytom, thanks for the quick reply

```
DEBUG starship::config > STARSHIP_CONFIG is not set
 DEBUG starship::config > Using default config path: /home/u/.config/starship.toml
 DEBUG starship::config > Unable to parse the config file: failed to parse datetime for key `add_newline` at line 1 column 15
 DEBUG starship::modules::directory > Current directory: "/home/u"
 DEBUG starship::modules::directory > Dir string: ~
```

It was an error in my toml config format. Namely the value needing a lowercase boolean True. Since it is obviously not a bug related to symbolic links, but me not knowing the toml syntax, the issue can be closed.

Still should I not expect as a first time user that the application would error on failing to parse the config instead of silently ignoring it?

No problem, glad this solved your problem

> Still should I not expect as a first time user that the application would error on failing to parse the config instead of silently ignoring it?

This is something we are aware of and will hopefully be fixed in the near future, see #1075 for more information.
